houdini_version_notes: APEX RunVex uses named inputs/outputs and has NO @ attribute syntax.
title: Blend Two Vectors (RunVex)
prompt: Linearly blend two vectors by a factor inside an APEX RunVex node
explanation: APEX RunVex behaves like a Snippet VOP but binds named inputs and outputs instead of geometry attributes, so there is no '@' syntax. Here it simply interpolates between two vector inputs by t.

title: Clamp a Control Value (RunVex)
prompt: Clamp a rig control value into a range in APEX
code:
// APEX RunVex. Inputs: float value, lo, hi. Output: float result.
result = clamp(value, lo, hi);
explanation: A minimal RunVex clamp, useful for bounding a driven rig control (e.g. a corrective blendshape weight) so animators cannot push it out of its valid range.

title: Smoothstep Easing (RunVex)
prompt: Ease a 0-1 control with a smoothstep curve in APEX
code:
// APEX RunVex. Input: float t in [0,1]. Output: float result.
result = smooth(0.0, 1.0, t);
explanation: smooth() is VEX's smoothstep: it eases a value with zero slope at both ends. In a rig it softens the response of a driven control so motion starts and stops gently.

houdini_version_notes: Named inputs/outputs; no @ syntax. translate()/scale() modify the matrix in place.
title: Compose a Transform Matrix (RunVex)
prompt: Build a 4x4 transform from a translation and uniform scale in APEX
explanation: Starting from the identity, scale() then translate() mutate the matrix in place to build a TRS transform. Emitting it as a named matrix output lets downstream APEX nodes apply it to a joint or control.

title: Remap a Control Range (RunVex)
prompt: Remap a rig control from one range to another in APEX
explanation: fit() linearly remaps a value between input and output ranges -- the workhorse of driven-key style rigging, e.g. turning a slider's 0-10 range into a joint's -45..45 degrees.

houdini_version_notes: Named inputs/outputs; no @ syntax. Euler angles in radians, XYZ order.
title: Euler to Quaternion (RunVex)
prompt: Convert euler angles to a quaternion in APEX
code:
// APEX RunVex. Input: vector euler (radians). Output: vector4 q.
q = eulertoquaternion(euler, 0);   // 0 = XYZ rotation order
explanation: eulertoquaternion() converts per-axis euler angles into a single quaternion, which is the rotation form most APEX joint operations expect. The second argument selects the rotation order.
